newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise in quiet, thin market.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise in quiet, thin market.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late Wednesday, lifted by Wall Street.
The market opened flat but some slim buyer interest was sufficient to extend Tuesday's rally. Traders said there was still very thin activity, as investors remained on the sidelines.
"Uncertainty on U.S. rates is still here for the medium-term," said a trader.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/4 to 89-1/2, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 rose $0.10 to 124.80 Tuesday.

Traders did not expect the market to break out of its recent ranges any time soon, particularly as the uncertainty on U.S. rates was seen lasting at least until May, when the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee next meets.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 5.90 percent from 5.88 percent.
